response:
Diagnosis after generation 5. The frontier has split into three distinguishable designs: (a) the gen-1 industry-neutral composite still has the best joint profile (fmb −4.20, alpha −3.7%, t=−2.98); (b) IND_RANK gave the best slope (−4.23) but a weaker alpha (−2.6%, t=−2.03), telling me rank compression helps pooled regression fit but throws away the tail magnitude the portfolio needs, so z-scores remain the right choice for alpha; (c) the new payout-overreach leg produced the best reliability in the archive (alpha −3.4%, t=−3.06) with good coverage. Crucially, the two best-alpha financing legs of the last two rounds — (netfin − ib)/at and (dvt + prstkc − ib)/at — both subtract earnings, and paired with an accrual leg that already subtracts operating cash flow they jointly lean on firms with deeply negative operating cash generation. That suggests the alpha may be coming from a *cash-flow-deficit-plus-external-funding* mechanism rather than from accrual aggressiveness per se, which I must test explicitly before consolidating further. This batch therefore includes that diagnostic, two constructions that combine the independently strong issuance and payout-overreach channels, a test of the correct coverage benchmark (earnings vs operating cash flow), a sharper capital-structure amplifier, and one new mechanism (debt-funded dividends). Note: dlc is shared across themes and cannot serve as the financing leg, so all financing legs here use theme-exclusive items.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: AccrualsWithFundingAndOverdistribution
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), RATIO(SUB(ADD(dvt, prstkc), ib), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Accrual-heavy firms are most overvalued when they simultaneously take in outside capital and distribute more than they earn, because the two flows together prove that reported profits are not funding either investment or the payout.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The net-financing leg gave the best cross-sectional slope while the payout-overreach leg gave the best FF5 reliability (t=−3.06), and these are economically distinct verification failures that have never been combined. Nesting them inside the financing leg preserves the accrual leg at 50% weight, which was the fix that prevented the third-leg dilution seen in generation 2.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: CashDeficitFinancingDiagnostic
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(NEG(RATIO(oancf, at))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: If the mechanism is that externally funded firms with weak cash generation are overpriced, then operating cash flow weakness alone, interacted with external financing, should carry the signal, and the earnings-minus-cash-flow accrual construction adds nothing.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: My best recent legs all subtract earnings and pair with an accrual measure that subtracts cash flow, so the archive cannot distinguish "aggressive accruals" from "negative operating cash flow" as the operative accounting-quality variable. This is a deliberately stripped-down diagnostic: if it matches the winner, later generations should build on cash-flow deficits; if it is clearly weaker, the accrual gap is doing real work and I can drop the earnings-subtraction variants.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: AccrualsWithPayoutBeyondCashFlow
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dvt, prstkc), oancf), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Payout sustainability should be judged against cash actually generated, not against accrual-based earnings, so distributions in excess of operating cash flow identify the firms that must return to the capital markets or deplete the balance sheet.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The gen-5 payout-overreach leg benchmarked distributions against ib and produced the archive's most reliable alpha; benchmarking against oancf is the economically correct coverage test and isolates whether that leg worked because of the payout information or because subtracting earnings loaded on low profitability. Keeping the accrual leg unchanged makes the comparison a single-choice experiment.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: EquityCushionAmplifiedAccruals
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(lt, ceq)))
HYPOTHESIS: What amplifies accrual mispricing is how little equity capital stands behind the outside claims: with a thin equity cushion, an accrual reversal transfers value to creditors and forces distressed financing.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Leverage measured as lt/at raised the alpha to −4.0% when added as a third leg but diluted the accrual weight; the debt-to-equity form is a sharper measure of cushion depletion and here it is used as a full 50% leg rather than a diluting third. This tests the balance-sheet-pressure interpretation against the market-timing interpretation with no issuance flow present at all.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: AccrualsPayoutOverreachIssuanceSpike
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dvt, prstkc), ib), at), TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), at), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: The most fragile configuration is an accrual-heavy firm distributing beyond its earnings while raising an unusual amount of capital relative to its own funding history — over-distribution and opportunistic replacement funding at the same time.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The two highest-reliability portfolio legs in the archive are payout overreach (t=−3.06) and own-history issuance spikes (Sharpe −0.53), and each addresses a different weakness of the other: payout overreach is level-based and type-driven, the spike is event-based and firm-relative. Combining them inside the financing leg tests whether the archive's portfolio evidence can be pushed materially past t=−3 without sacrificing the slope.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: DebtFundedDividendsWithAccruals
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(MIN(DELTA(dltt, 1), dvc), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Borrowing while paying dividends is a specific and costly signal of managerial commitment to an unsustainable payout; when reported earnings are also accrual-inflated, the dividend is effectively being funded by creditors and the equity is overpriced.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: MIN(DELTA(dltt), dvc) captures the overlap of the two flows, so the leg only becomes large when a firm genuinely increased long-term debt *and* paid a substantial dividend, which no prior leg isolates — issuance volumes and payout levels were always measured separately. This is a distinct economic mechanism (creditor-financed distributions) rather than a restatement of financing intensity.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
